articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft's April patch bonanza includes 167 vulnerabilities with a SharePoint zero-day and BlueHammer in Windows Defender. Nothing says 'Patch Tuesday' like a security apocalypse served with your morning coffee.

articles.title: Silver Fox Springs Tax-Themed Attacks on Orgs in India, Russia
articles.summary: Critical cPanel authentication bypass flaw has multiple PoCs in the wild, with researchers claiming zero-day activity for at least a month. When your control panel becomes someone else's control panel, you're having a bad time.

articles.title: US CISA adds ‘insane’ Linux Copy Fail flaw to watch list
articles.summary: CISA adds actively exploited Linux root access bug CVE-2026-31431 to KEV catalog. Because sometimes the penguin bites back, and apparently it's been biting for a while now.

articles.title: ADT data breach exposes customer information
articles.summary: Cybersecurity firm Trellix suffers source code breach with unauthorized repository access. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a poorly secured API key.

articles.title: What is hacking? Types, techniques, and how to protect yourself
articles.summary: ADT data breach exposes customer information including names, phone numbers, and addresses, with ShinyHunters claiming millions of records stolen. Your home security company just became everyone else's open door.

articles.title: RMM Tools Fuel Stealthy Phishing Campaign
articles.summary: Public records laws revealed ALPR surveillance abuse, so now states want to block what the public sees. Classic move: when transparency exposes your overreach, just kill the transparency.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's new anti-VPN law takes effect, because nothing says 'freedom' like banning the tools that protect it. Expect VPN usage to surge faster than a Mormon missionary on Red Bull.

articles.title: Getting Digital Fairness Right: EFF's Recommendations for the EU's Digital Fairness Act
articles.summary: EFF submits feedback on UK's digital ID scheme, because what could possibly go wrong with the government that brought you the Online Safety Act managing your digital identity?

articles.title: Week in review: High-severity LPE vulnerability in the Linux kernel, cPanel 0-day exploited for months
articles.summary: Citizen Lab exposes sophisticated telecom surveillance campaigns by commercial surveillance vendors exploiting mobile operator infrastructure. Your phone calls have been brought to you by the surveillance-industrial complex.

articles.title: EFF Submission to UK Consultation on Digital ID
articles.summary: Germany doxxes 'UNKN,' the Russian mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware gangs, revealing 31-year-old Daniil Shchukin's face. When your OPSEC fails harder than your ransomware victims' backups.
